_README: THE EQUIVALENCE CLASSIFICATION for capture-host's diff-scoped mutation gate.
Sibling of the repo-root tools/mutate-equivalence.json, same rules, same failure modes.
A surviving mutant is not automatically a test gap. Some cannot be killed by ANY input, because a
guard the mutation weakens is followed by code that rejects the same cases anyway. Leaving those
red forever is how mutate_diff.py's own header says a gate dies ('trains people to ignore it');
waving them through in a PR comment is how it starts lying. This file is the third option.
KEYED ON THE MUTANT'S DIFF (its -/+ line pair, whitespace-normalised) — never on mutmut's
__mutmut_N index, which renumbers whenever anything earlier in the function changes and would
silently start excusing a different mutation.
THE CLASSES, and they are not interchangeable:
no-distinguishing-input  a battery of inputs was run against original and mutant and every one
agreed. STRONG EVIDENCE, NOT PROOF: a proof needs an argument over the
whole domain. `probe` records what was actually run so the claim can be
re-checked or widened.
untestable-by-design     a log string, or a branch unreachable by construction. The argument in
`why` must be about the CODE, not about the test suite.
real-gap                 killable, no test yet. STILL FAILS THE GATE. Debt, not an excuse.
THIS FILE CANNOT FLATTER THE VERDICT. mutate_diff.py reports three states loudly:
REFUTED   an entry claims equivalence and the mutant was KILLED. The claim is wrong; fix the
ENTRY, never the test. This FAILS the gate — it is the only way a stale file could
hide a real gap.
ORPHANED  an entry matches no generated mutant (the line moved). Excluded from every count, so
a stale entry shrinks nothing.
unclassified survivors fail the gate exactly as before. Silence is never equivalence.

probe_verity_survey.py.key: - if not (len(tail) == 6 and tail.isdigit()): | + if not (len(tail) == 6 or tail.isdigit()):
probe_verity_survey.py.why: The weakened guard lets through exactly two extra shapes: len==6 but not all digits, and all digits but len!=6. Both then reach strptime(tail, '%H%M%S'), which raises ValueError for either, and the except returns False — the same value the guard would have returned. The guard is a fast path, not a semantic gate, so no input can separate them.
probe_verity_survey.py.probe: 133,495 directory names: 26,699 tails (lengths 0-8 over digits+letters+' -:.', plus the hand-picked 120059/995959/9999XX/12345/1234567/240000/000000/235959/00000/0000000) crossed with 5 prefixes (dated matching, dated non-matching, undated, bare, three-part). Original vs mutant differed on 0.

probe_polar_usb.py.why: `initial` is read in exactly ONE place — `reply_body(rep, initial)`, whose body is `off = _HDR_FIRST if initial else _HDR_REST`. That is a truthiness test, and `bool(False) == bool(None) == False`, so both values select the same branch by construction rather than by coincidence. No report can separate them: the variable never reaches a comparison, an arithmetic operator, a return value or the result dict.
probe_polar_usb.py.probe: Exhaustive over the shape space of a 64-byte HID report: size 0..63 x flags 0..3 = 256 report shapes, each passed to reply_body() with `False` and with `None`. 0 of 256 differed. Widening it is pointless — the argument is consumed by `if initial` and nothing else.

probe_polar_usb.py.key: - while real + idle < max_packets and time.monotonic() < deadline: | + while real + idle < max_packets and time.monotonic() <= deadline:
probe_polar_usb.py.why: `<` and `<=` differ on exactly one point of the domain: `time.monotonic() == deadline` EXACTLY, as floats. `deadline` is computed once from an earlier `monotonic()` read plus a window, and the clock advances monotonically at nanosecond resolution between the two reads — so hitting it requires a later read to land bit-identically on a value derived from an earlier one. A test cannot arrange it without patching the clock, and patching the clock to a fixed value would make the loop condition constant and test nothing about the deadline. Note the consequence even IF it occurred is one extra loop iteration, which the `max_packets` bound and the `select` timeout both still cap.
probe_polar_usb.py.probe: 2,000,000 consecutive `time.monotonic()` reads compared against a deadline captured before the loop: 0 exact matches. `time.get_clock_info('monotonic').resolution` is 1e-09 s on this platform.

polar_pmd.py.key: - fs = fs or SAMPLE_HZ.get(meas, 0) or 1 | + fs = fs or SAMPLE_HZ.get(meas, None) or 1
polar_pmd.py.why: The .get default is only consulted for a meas ABSENT from SAMPLE_HZ, and decode_frame raises ValueError('not decoded') for every such meas before the value is ever spent. So the default is unreachable; and even where it were reached, 0 and None are both falsy and the trailing `or 1` maps them to the same 1.
polar_pmd.py.probe: Enumerated SAMPLE_HZ: every decodable meas (ECG/PPG/ACC/GYRO/MAG/PPI) is a KEY, so .get hits and the default is never used. Drove decode_frame over 80 frame/fs/prev_last_ns combinations (4 meas x 4 fs incl. None x 5 prev) — the default is consulted 0 times. An unknown meas (0x3E) raises before reaching it.

polar_pmd.py.key: - fs = fs or SAMPLE_HZ.get(meas, 0) or 1 | + fs = fs or SAMPLE_HZ.get(meas, ) or 1
polar_pmd.py.why: Dropping the default makes .get return None on a miss — falsy, so the trailing `or 1` yields the same 1 as the falsy 0 it replaced. And the miss branch is unreachable anyway (see mutmut_26).
polar_pmd.py.probe: Same 80-combination battery. SAMPLE_HZ.get(PPI, 0) or 1 == SAMPLE_HZ.get(PPI) or 1 == 1.

polar_pmd.py.key: - fs = fs or SAMPLE_HZ.get(meas, 0) or 1 | + fs = fs or SAMPLE_HZ.get(meas, 1) or 1
polar_pmd.py.why: A default of 1 is truthy so `or 1` is skipped, but the value is 1 either way. Identical result, and the branch is unreachable regardless.
polar_pmd.py.probe: Same 80-combination battery; SAMPLE_HZ.get(PPI, 1) or 1 == 1 == SAMPLE_HZ.get(PPI, 0) or 1.

polar_pmd.py.key: - fs = fs or SAMPLE_HZ.get(meas, 0) or 1 | + fs = fs or SAMPLE_HZ.get(meas, 0) or 2
polar_pmd.py.why: The `or` fallback fires only when SAMPLE_HZ[meas] is falsy, and PPI (rate 0) is the ONLY such meas. PPI frames set ppi=True, which forces back=0 for every sample, so step_ns is computed and never spent — no output byte depends on whether the fallback is 1 or 2.
polar_pmd.py.probe: [k for k,v in SAMPLE_HZ.items() if not v] == [3] (PPI). Decoded PPI frames with fs=None at both fallbacks: sensor_ns, t_ms, phone and values byte-identical, because `back = 0 if ppi else (n-1-i)`.

polar_pmd.py.why: `truncated` is a local consumed only by `if truncated: raise`. None and False are both falsy, so the raise fires identically and no caller can observe which was assigned — the name never leaves the function.
polar_pmd.py.probe: 455-case battery, `tools/probe_equivalence.py --module polar_pmd.py` (committed, re-runnable): 7 frame shapes x 5 fs (None/52/130/176/1000) x 13 prev_last_ns including the EXACT 0.9x / 1.0x / 1.1x / 0.5x / 1.5x nominal boundaries per fs, plus 0, 1, 3 and n ns. Compared sensor_ns, phone and values byte-for-byte; 0/455 differ. The battery's canaries all fire (sign flip 150/455, PPI >>8 65/455, 1.1-strict 6/455, clamp-lower 45/455), so a zero here is a measurement, not a blind spot — an earlier 160-case battery returned 0 for two of those canaries and was rejected.

polar_pmd.py.key: - if prev_last_ns is not None and n > 0: | + if prev_last_ns is not None and n > 1:
polar_pmd.py.why: The guard only gates computing `step_ns` from the device clock. At n == 1 the single sample has back = 0, so neither `sensor_ns` (last_ns - 0) nor `phone` (arrival - 0) depends on step_ns. The branch is reachable at n == 1 and changes nothing observable there; at n == 0 both forms skip it.

polar_pmd.py.key: - if 0.9 * step_ns <= est <= 1.1 * step_ns: # a dropped frame / restart inflates est — keep nominal | + if 0.9 / step_ns <= est <= 1.1 * step_ns: # a dropped frame / restart inflates est — keep nominal
polar_pmd.py.why: Replacing the lower bound with 0.9/step_ns makes it ~1e-7 ns, so the if-branch now also accepts every est in (0, 0.9*step). But the ELIF below (`0 < est < step_ns`) already assigned `step_ns = est` for exactly that range, so the same value is assigned by a different branch. Above 1.1*step both forms refuse; at or below 0 both refuse.

polar_pmd.py.key: - if 0.9 * step_ns <= est <= 1.1 * step_ns: # a dropped frame / restart inflates est — keep nominal | + if 0.9 * step_ns < est <= 1.1 * step_ns: # a dropped frame / restart inflates est — keep nominal
polar_pmd.py.why: Differs only when est == 0.9*step_ns exactly. There the strict form falls to the elif `0 < est < step_ns`, which is true (0.9*step < step) and assigns the identical `step_ns = est`. Probed at that exact boundary for every fs, including fs=1000 where 0.9*nominal*n is an exact integer.

polar_pmd.py.key: - elif 0 < est < step_ns: | + elif 0 < est <= step_ns:
polar_pmd.py.why: Differs only when est == step_ns exactly — and that value is already inside [0.9*step, 1.1*step], so the IF above matched first and the elif is never reached. Unreachable difference.

polar_pmd.py.why: A 1e-9 relative change to the divisor. The largest back*step_ns in any real frame is ~a few hundred ms, so the delta is ~1e-10 s — four orders below datetime's 1 us resolution, which quantises it away before it can be observed.
